title: Category bar complex and functorial derived colimits
statement:
Let $\mathcal E$ be a small category in the universe of [def-weil-size-convention], endowed with the topology generated by singleton identity coverings (equivalently the pretopology of singleton isomorphisms), so all presheaves are sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For a commutative ring $R$, let $\underline R$ be the constant ring presheaf and $\operatorname{Mod}(\underline R)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal E^{op},\operatorname{Mod}(R))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The morphism $\pi_{\mathcal E}^R:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal E),\underline R)\to(*,R)$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] has inverse image the constant-presheaf functor, identity structural map, and left adjoint $\pi_{\mathcal E,!}^R(F)=\operatorname{colim}_{\mathcal E^{op}}F$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Its total left derived functor $L\pi_{\mathcal E,!}^R:D(\underline R)\to D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] exists (it is defined at every object in the sense of [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization]), is triangulated, and is left adjoint to the exact constant-presheaf functor. For a module presheaf $F$ in degree zero it is canonically represented by the cochain complex $K_{\mathcal E}(F)$ with
$$K_{\mathcal E}(F)^{-n}=\bigoplus_{U_n\to\cdots\to U_0}F(U_0)\quad(n\geq0),\qquad K_{\mathcal E}(F)^r=0\quad(r>0).$$
Its differential is $\sum_{j=0}^n(-1)^j d_j$: face $d_j$ deletes $U_{n-j}$, composing the adjacent arrows at an internal vertex; if $j<n$ it retains the element of $F(U_0)$, and the last face $d_n$ applies the restriction $F(U_1\to U_0)$. Thus for $n=2$ the differential is $(U_1\to U_0,x)-(U_2\to U_0,x)+(U_2\to U_1,x|_{U_1})$. The functor $K_{\mathcal E}$ takes every objectwise short exact sequence of module presheaves to a degreewise short exact sequence of complexes. For a functor $u:\mathcal E\to\mathcal F$, a ring map $R\to S$, a module presheaf $F$ over $R$ on $\mathcal E$, a module presheaf $G$ over $S$ on $\mathcal F$, and a semilinear natural map $t:F\to u^{-1}G$, the canonical derived-colimit map is represented, after restriction of scalars to $R$, by
$$(U_n\to\cdots\to U_0,x)\longmapsto(uU_n\to\cdots\to uU_0,t_{U_0}(x)).$$
Here $u^{-1}$ is precomposition. These maps preserve identities and composition and commute with the connecting morphisms of short exact sequences. For parallel functors $v,w:\mathcal E\to\mathcal F$, a natural transformation $\eta:v\Rightarrow w$, and $t:F\to w^{-1}G$, the two maps $K(v,G(\eta)t)$ and $K(w,t)$ are chain homotopic and hence equal in $D(R)$. Here $(G(\eta)t)_U=G(\eta_U)t_U$. In particular a natural isomorphism of indexing functors induces the same derived map after the corresponding coefficient identifications.

proof.text: Use the topology generated by singleton identity coverings, equivalently the pretopology of singleton isomorphisms. The sheaf condition for an isomorphism is automatic, so the module category is exactly the presheaf category in the statement. Kernels and cokernels are objectwise by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The constant functor preserves finite limits and has right adjoint the limit: a map from a constant object is precisely a compatible family of maps to all values. It therefore defines the stated geometric morphism with identity ring map. The required colimit exists explicitly: quotient $\bigoplus_UF(U)$ by the submodule generated by $\iota_Ux-\iota_VF(a)x$ for $a:V\to U$. Compatible families of linear maps are exactly maps out of this quotient. A map $F\to\underline M$ is precisely a cocone from $F$ to $M$, so [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] identifies its left adjoint with $\operatorname{colim}_{\mathcal E^{op}}$.

source.place: Tag 08PF, example-category-to-point; colimit adjunction written from its universal property.

proof.text: The projection $\mathcal E\to *$ is continuous: isomorphisms and their pullbacks are carried to isomorphisms and their pullbacks. It is cocontinuous: the only covering of the point needed in the singleton-isomorphism pretopology is refined by $\{1_U\}$ for each $U$. All indexing sets are small in [def-weil-size-convention]. Apply [lem-trf-continuous-cocontinuous-derived-shriek] with $\mathcal O=R$ to get the unbounded triangulated $L\pi_!$ and its adjunction to the exact constant functor. The same argument applies to any functor between categories with these topologies. For $u:\mathcal E\to\mathcal F$ it supplies $Lu_!$, adjoint to precomposition. Since the inverse images satisfy $\pi_{\mathcal E}^{-1}=u^{-1}\pi_{\mathcal F}^{-1}$, the Hom adjunctions identify $L\pi_{\mathcal F,!}Lu_!$ with $L\pi_{\mathcal E,!}$, with the composite adjunction unit and counit.

source.place: Tags 07AC, lemma-existence-derived-lower-shriek, and 08PH, example-morphism-categories; composition follows by composing the displayed adjunction bijections.

proof.text: For $U\in\mathcal E$ and an $R$-module $M$, define $L_U(M)(V)=\bigoplus_{a:V\to U}M$, restrictions sending the $a$-summand to the $a\circ b$-summand. A map $L_U(M)\to H$ is uniquely determined by its value on the identity summand at $U$: its value on $(a,m)$ must be $H(a)(f(m))$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}(L_U(M),H)=\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,H(U))$. It follows directly from the lifting definition that $L_U(P)$ is projective when $P$ is a projective module. Every module has a free epimorphism, and $\bigoplus_{U,x\in H(U)}L_U(R)\to H$, $(a,r)\mapsto rH(a)(x)$, is surjective at $V$ because $x\in H(V)$ is hit by $(1_V,1)$. Direct sums of these projectives are projective: choose each lift and take their coproduct. Hence both module categories used below have enough projectives. Direct sums are exact: every element has finite support, and an element in a componentwise kernel has preimages in those finitely many components. In particular each $L_U$ is exact. The colimit universal property gives $\pi_!L_U(M)=M$, with every $a$-summand mapping identically to $M$.

source.place: Tag 08PG, example-left-derived-colimits: the representable generators, made explicit for arbitrary coefficient modules.

proof.text: Construct an augmented presheaf complex $B(F)$ by $B_n(F)=\bigoplus_{U_n\to\cdots\to U_0}L_{U_n}(F(U_0))$ in degree $-n$. At $V$ a generator is $(V\xrightarrow a U_n\to\cdots\to U_0,x)$. The first face removes $U_n$ and composes $a$ with the next arrow, internal faces compose adjacent arrows, and the last face removes $U_0$ and restricts $x$ to $U_1$. Use the alternating signs in the statement. The augmentation $B_0(F)(V)\to F(V)$ is $(a:V\to U_0,x)\mapsto F(a)x$. Deleting two vertices in either order yields the same generator and coefficient: for internal vertices this is associativity, and at the coefficient end it is $F(ab)=F(b)F(a)$. Thus $d_i d_j=d_{j-1}d_i$ for $i<j$; the corresponding two terms of $d^2$ have opposite signs. This proves $d^2=0$ and compatibility with the augmentation.

source.place: Tag 08PG, example-left-derived-colimits; explicit presheaf resolution realizing its alternating category-chain formula.

proof.text: At a fixed $V$, insert $V$ at the left of the displayed chain: $s_n(V\xrightarrow a U_n\to\cdots\to U_0,x)=(V\xrightarrow{1}V\xrightarrow a U_n\to\cdots\to U_0,x)$, and $s_{-1}(x)=(1_V,x)$. Deleting the inserted vertex is the identity, while every other deletion is insertion after the corresponding old deletion. Therefore $ds_n+s_{n-1}d=1$ on the augmented complex, also in degree zero, where the extra term is $s_{-1}\varepsilon$. Consequently $B(F)(V)\to F(V)[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism for every $V$. Kernels and cokernels are objectwise, so $B(F)\to F[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism of module presheaves. This contraction is asserted only after evaluation; it need not be a natural presheaf contraction.

source.place: Tag 08PG, example-left-derived-colimits: fills in the omitted contraction verification, on the augmented presheaf bar resolution.

proof.text: Fix a chain-indexed family of modules $M_c$ and objects $U_c$. By [lem-trf-bounded-above-acyclic-derived-computation], choose projective module resolutions $P_c\to M_c[0]$, all zero in positive degrees. The complex $\bigoplus_c L_{U_c}(P_c)$ is a projective resolution of $\bigoplus_c L_{U_c}(M_c)$: exactness and projectivity were proved in step 3. Applying $\pi_!$ gives $\bigoplus_cP_c\to(\bigoplus_cM_c)[0]$, which is a quasi-isomorphism by the same finite-support calculation. Projective computation in the cited node therefore shows that every $\bigoplus_c L_{U_c}(M_c)$ is left $\pi_!$-acyclic. Similarly, for $u:\mathcal E\to\mathcal F$, the adjunction calculation of step 3 gives $u_!L_U(M)=L_{uU}(M)$: their Hom sets into $G$ are both $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,G(uU))$. Applying $u_!$ to the same projective resolution gives an exact resolution $\bigoplus_cL_{uU_c}(P_c)$, so these objects are also left $u_!$-acyclic.

source.place: Tag 08PG, example-left-derived-colimits; projective resolution argument extending the representable contraction to arbitrary modules; derived.tex Tags 0646, 06XN and dual 015E.

proof.text: Each term of $B(F)$ has the form in step 6, and $B(F)$ is bounded above by zero. Apply [lem-trf-bounded-above-acyclic-derived-computation] to its quasi-isomorphic augmentation from step 5. This gives the canonical identification $L\pi_!F\simeq\pi_!B(F)$. Step 3 identifies the latter's degree $-n$ with $\bigoplus_{U_n\to\cdots\to U_0}F(U_0)$. Its faces are exactly the stated faces, since a morphism between the representable factors becomes the identity on the coefficient after colimit. In degree two they are precisely the three summands displayed in the statement. The derived comparison in the cited node makes this a natural identification in $F$, not merely an equality of homology groups.

source.place: Tag 08PG, example-left-derived-colimits; upgrading the chain calculation to its canonical derived-category model by bounded above acyclic computation.

proof.text: For $0\to F'\to F\to F''\to0$ objectwise exact, every degree of $K$ is a direct sum, over the same set of chains, of the exact sequence at $U_0$. The finite-support argument of step 3 proves injectivity, kernel equality and surjectivity of that direct sum. All coefficient maps commute with restriction, so this is a short exact sequence of complexes. The identical argument also gives a short exact sequence of presheaf bar resolutions $B(F')\to B(F)\to B(F'')$.

source.place: Tag 08PG, example-left-derived-colimits, short-exact-sequence assertion, with the finite-support justification.

proof.text: First work over a single ring $R$. Given $t:F\to u^{-1}G$, send a generator of $B_{\mathcal E}(F)(V)$ to $(uV\xrightarrow{u(a)}uU_n\to\cdots\to uU_0,t_{U_0}x)$ in $B_{\mathcal F}(G)(uV)$. This commutes with the augmentation by naturality of $t$. It commutes with every face: functoriality of $u$ handles compositions, and the coefficient face is exactly $t_{U_1}F(U_1\to U_0)=G(uU_1\to uU_0)t_{U_0}$. By adjunction this gives $u_!B_{\mathcal E}(F)\to B_{\mathcal F}(G)$. Step 6 and [lem-trf-bounded-above-acyclic-derived-computation] identify its source with $Lu_!F$ and its target with $G$, compatibly with the augmentations. Thus it represents the derived adjunct $Lu_!F\to G$ of $t$. Applying $L\pi_{\mathcal F,!}$, and the composite adjunction of step 2, gives the canonical map of Tag 08PD. That identification is computed on these models: by the explicit adjunction clause of [lem-trf-continuous-cocontinuous-derived-shriek] (take $f=\mathrm{id}$, then compose with $\varepsilon_C^{-1}$), at a complex $C$ with $\varepsilon_C$ invertible the derived unit is $g^{-1}(\varepsilon_C^{-1})\circ Q(C\to g^{-1}g_!C)$. Hence on $B_{\mathcal E}(F)$ the derived units of $L\pi_{\mathcal E,!}$ and of $L\pi_{\mathcal F,!}Lu_!$ are both represented by the termwise unit $B_{\mathcal E}(F)\to\pi_{\mathcal E}^{-1}\pi_{\mathcal E,!}B_{\mathcal E}(F)=u^{-1}\pi_{\mathcal F}^{-1}\pi_{\mathcal F,!}u_!B_{\mathcal E}(F)$, so the step-2 isomorphism is the identity of $K_{\mathcal E}(F)$ on the models of step 7. Both complexes of representable sums are $\pi_{\mathcal F,!}$-acyclic by step 6; the cited comparison therefore computes this map by applying ordinary $\pi_{\mathcal F,!}$ to the displayed map. Its formula is precisely $(U_\bullet,x)\mapsto(uU_\bullet,t_{U_0}x)$.

source.place: Tags 08PD, remark-morphism-fibred-categories, and 08PH, example-morphism-categories; the map is computed on explicit augmented acyclic resolutions.

proof.text: For $R\to S$, replace $G$ temporarily by its restriction $\operatorname{Res}_R^S G$. Restriction changes neither underlying abelian groups nor any differential or direct sum, so $B_R(\operatorname{Res}G)=\operatorname{Res}B_S(G)$ and $K_R(\operatorname{Res}G)=\operatorname{Res}K_S(G)$ by their displayed formulas. Their augmentations are the same maps. The acyclicity proofs of steps 3 and 6 apply over both rings separately; [lem-trf-bounded-above-acyclic-derived-computation] identifies these complexes with their respective derived colimits. This supplies the canonical scalar-restriction identification, and step 9 gives exactly the requested semilinear chain map under it. No assertion that restriction preserves projectives, and no flatness of $S$ over $R$, is used.

source.place: Tags 08PG and 08PH, same explicit resolutions after restriction of coefficient scalars; coefficient refinement written by Q71.

proof.text: For identity functor and identity coefficient map, each generator is unchanged. Composing $(u,t)$ and $(v,s)$ sends $(U_\bullet,x)$ first to $(uU_\bullet,t_{U_0}x)$ and then to $(vuU_\bullet,s_{uU_0}t_{U_0}x)$, exactly the formula for the composite coefficient map. These are equal chain maps before localization. Therefore they give the identity and composition laws for the canonical derived maps of steps 9 and 10. The argument works also for composable coefficient-ring maps because the same underlying maps are used at every restriction of scalars.

source.place: Tag 08PH, example-morphism-categories, identity and composition checked on the generators.

proof.text: Connecting morphisms are compatible as well. For a short exact sequence of complexes $A\xrightarrow i B\xrightarrow p C$, the chain map $q:\operatorname{Cone}(i)\to C$, $(b,a)\mapsto p(b)$, is a quasi-isomorphism: its kernel has terms $A^r\oplus A^{r+1}$ and differential $(a,a')\mapsto(da+a',-da')$, contracted by $(a,a')\mapsto(0,a)$. The connecting morphism is represented by the roof $C\xleftarrow q\operatorname{Cone}(i)\xrightarrow{-\mathrm{pr}}A[1]$, using [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]'s cone convention. A morphism of short exact sequences induces the map $(b,a)\mapsto(f_Bb,f_Aa)$ on these cones; it commutes with $q$ and with $-\mathrm{pr}$. Apply this to the short exact sequences of $B$ and $K$ in step 8. The augmentation $B(F)\to F$ gives a morphism of such sequences. The natural comparisons in [lem-trf-bounded-above-acyclic-derived-computation] and triangulatedness of $L\pi_!$ therefore identify the $K$-roof with the derived connecting morphism. The maps of step 9 give morphisms of the same roofs. Their squares with connecting morphisms commute already as roof diagrams. Exact scalar restriction preserves this calculation, proving the semilinear claim too.

source.place: Tags 08PG and 08PH; derived.tex cone convention and Tag 0152, lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor. Explicit cone-roof naturality, without invoking an uncited boundary-compatibility theorem.

proof.text:
For the natural transformation clause put $p_r$, $0\leq r\leq n$, for the map sending $(U_n\to\cdots\to U_0,x)$ to the length-$(n+1)$ chain
$$vU_n\to\cdots\to vU_{n-r}\xrightarrow{\eta_{U_{n-r}}}wU_{n-r}\to\cdots\to wU_0$$
with coefficient $t_{U_0}x\in G(wU_0)$. Define $H_n=\sum_{r=0}^n(-1)^rp_r:K_{\mathcal E}(F)^{-n}\to K_{\mathcal F}(G)^{-n-1}$ and $H_{-1}=0$. These maps are linear, also after scalar restriction. At the two ends $d_0p_0=K(w,t)$ and $d_{n+1}p_n=K(v,G(\eta)t)$: the last equality is precisely the restriction $G(\eta_{U_0})t_{U_0}$. At degree zero this says $dH_0(U,x)=(wU,t_Ux)-(vU,G(\eta_U)t_Ux)$.

source.place: Agent expansion of the natural-transformation extension of the chain formula in Tag 08PH: prism maps with the same vertex order and signs as Tag 08PG.

proof.text: For $j<r$, deleting a vertex before the inserted arrow gives $d_jp_r=p_{r-1}d_j$. For $j>r+1$, deleting after it gives $d_jp_r=p_rd_{j-1}$; at the coefficient end this uses the naturality of $t$. At the junction, for $0\leq r<n$, naturality $w(a)\eta_V=\eta_Uv(a)$ for $a:V\to U$ gives $d_{r+1}p_r=d_{r+1}p_{r+1}$. In $dH+Hd$ the first two kinds cancel because their signs are respectively $(-1)^{j+r}$ versus $(-1)^{j+r-1}$ and $(-1)^{j+r}$ versus $(-1)^{j+r-1}$. The junction terms cancel between $p_r$ and $p_{r+1}$. The only survivors are the two end terms of step 13, with signs $+1$ and $(-1)^n(-1)^{n+1}=-1$. Hence $dH+Hd=K(w,t)-K(v,G(\eta)t)$. This proves the stated chain homotopy, and [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] identifies homotopic maps after passage to the derived category. If $\eta$ is an isomorphism its coefficient maps are isomorphisms, giving the last assertion. All constructions use finite sums in each input generator, including identity arrows; they require no nonemptiness or finiteness of the categories.
